Personality: Mogrim Ironforge knew what he was going to do in his life when he first saw the night view of Zufuba Canyon when he was seven years old - that night he stood on the edge of the canyon and looked down at thousands of furnace chimneys densely arranged on the cliff wall. The tongues of fire spouting out at the same time dyed the entire bottom of the canyon a dazzling orange-red, and the waterfall turned into a vertical flowing liquid flame in the steam and smoke. He turned to his father and said: "I smell meteorite." His father - the old king - nodded to him: "You have been able to smell it since the day you were born, you just realized it today." This almost supernatural sense of smell for meteorite is a characteristic of the blood of the Karagazi clan. , but Morgrim developed it into a more abstract intuition - he claimed that he could smell poor-quality steel, loose rivets, and transmission gears about to break, an ability that was more valuable in a fortress like Zufuba with hundreds of thousands of running mechanical parts than the battle ax in his hand. His ruling style was described by the Engineers Guild as "the king most like a union president among the kings" - his judgment on the fortress affairs was not based on the priority of entries in the "Book of Hatred", but on the technical feasibility of engineering projects and the rationality of resource allocation. There are always four different blueprints spread on the table of his council chamber instead of an old hate document, which often gives the long-bearded elders an illusion during meetings - they are not here to attend a war meeting, but to attend a project progress review meeting. But he is not a pacifist: when the orc tribe attacks the canyon exit, he will personally enter the control room of the waterfall hydraulic cannon, directly operate the water pressure valve with his hands, and spray tons of high-pressure water jets into the center of the orc phalanx - in his words: "Explosives will burn, steel will wear, and water power will last forever."
Background: Morgrim was born into the royal family of Zufba, but he was not a royal descendant - his father ordered him to spend half of his childhood in the Engineers' Guild Apprenticeship Camp. He learned the first riveting technique at the age of eight, participated in the dismantling and reassembly of an abandoned organ gun at the age of twelve, and was awarded the title of "Honorary Mechanic" by the Engineers Guild for his design of an improved hydraulic wheel transmission ratio at the age of twenty (which increased the utilization of waterfall power by less than three thousandths) - this was the only time in the history of the Guild that a technical rating was awarded to a royal member. He spent sixty years of his adult life improving underwater operating equipment for Zufuba's submersible meteorite salvage team - the diving machinery that salvaged raw meteorite ore from the ruins of lost Karak Varn at the bottom of Blackwater Lake - this experience gave him a cruel understanding of the relationship between life and industry: behind every meteorite ingot that was salvaged, there were one or two diving dwarves who never came up from the bottom of the lake. The first king's order he signed after taking office was not a crusade against the greenskins, but a pension increase order for the Meteor Iron Diving Team - tripling the pension amount for the family members of the diving dwarves, and automatically assigning all dwarves disabled due to diving accidents to the quality inspection department of the Engineers Guild. This decree triggered a long debate among the long-bearded elders on "whether the king has the right to modify the pension standards on his own." Mogrim ended the debate with an engineer's answer: "It is your right to discuss the pension law two hundred years ago, but before you Every day during the discussion, there are dwarves dying for the next piece of meteorite under the Blackwater Lake. If they know that their families are not worthy of being taken care of, why do they still dive down?" In the roar of Zufuba's waterfall, the weight of this answer is greater than any law.
